svg.data-chapters: [{"t":0.35,"text":"Turning the handle spins a coil of wire between two magnets"},{"t":3.47,"text":"Wire moving through a magnetic field gets a current"},{"t":6.59,"text":"Each half turn the current reverses: alternating current"},{"t":9.71,"text":"Slip rings pass it to the circuit, and the lamp lights"}]
svg.font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How a generator makes alternating current

g.data-info: The north pole. The magnetic field runs from here across the gap to the south pole.

text.font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

g.data-info: A loop of wire on a shaft. As it turns, its sides cut through the magnetic field, and that pushes a current round the loop.
The south pole. Between the two poles the field is steady; nothing here moves.

text.font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

g.data-info: The current heats the filament. It is brightest twice in every turn, whichever way the current flows.
The needle shows the direction of the current: one way for half a turn, the other way for the next half.
